q: mapping 里 keyword 类型和 text 类型的关键区别是？

Keyword can only store numeric-typed data and text can only store string-typed data

The two are completely equivalent under the hood, just named differently by convention

why: id、作者名这类要精确匹配的字段用 keyword（想成 hash 表）；标题这类要判断「是否包含某词」的字段用 text，会被分词进倒排索引。

Both can store strings; the real difference isn't data type, it's whether the value gets tokenized into the inverted index.
There's no universal winner: keyword is usually cheaper for exact filters, while text is what you need for substring/full-text queries.

q: 写入返回的 _version 字段配合 ?version=N 更新，实现的是什么机制？

服务端自动合并两个并发写入的冲突内容
只是写入成功后的持久化确认回执而已
options_en: Pessimistic locking that must lock the entire document before it can be written
Optimistic concurrency control: a version mismatch fails the write for the client to retry
The server automatically merges the conflicting content of two concurrent writes
Merely a durability acknowledgment sent back after the write succeeds
why: 带版本条件的更新只在版本匹配时生效，否则抛错——这是乐观并发控制的典型例子，把冲突交给客户端重试。
why_en: Conditional updates on the version field are optimistic concurrency control: a mismatch fails the write and lets the client retry.

termDefinitions.meaning: Elasticsearch 给每个文档维护的版本号，配合乐观并发控制使用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The version field is a per-document counter Elasticsearch uses for optimistic concurrency control.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先假设不会冲突，写入时校验版本号，不匹配就报错让客户端重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic concurrency control assumes no conflict and lets a version mismatch fail the write for the client to retry.

q_en: What mechanism do _version and ?version=N implement for updates?

持久化确认是另一件事，跟这里的版本校验无关。

这份数据当前配置了多少个副本
options_en: How hot the physical data-center room actually runs that day
How much disk the shard occupies, with bigger shards pushed to colder tiers
How likely the data is to be queried, usually by recency, and whether it can still change
How many replicas this piece of data is currently configured with
why: 越新越常查的数据放 hot 层（好硬件），越旧越冷的数据下沉到 warm/cold/frozen——按访问概率和可变性分层省成本。
why_en: Data tiers are chosen by how likely the data is to be queried, usually by recency, and whether it can still change.

q_en: What determines hot, warm, cold, and frozen tiers for Data nodes?

optionExplanations_en: The layer names are just a metaphor for access patterns, not literal server-room temperature.
How much disk a shard uses isn't what decides its tier.
Tiering follows how likely the data is to be queried (how fresh it is) and whether it still changes, sinking colder data onto cheaper hardware.
Replica count is a separate setting, unrelated to which tier data sits in.

Never touching the source document and answering purely from indexed fields means the result is ready at the query stage, skipping the fetch cost entirely.

q: 补全 Elasticsearch 的「俄罗斯套娃」存储层级：

    I --> S2["Shard 1 (+副本)"]

Making an index no longer need a mapping defined at all, inferring every field type
Guaranteeing strong consistency across every shard and replica at every instant
why: 分片让数据和索引横向分布、查询并行化，是 ES 扩展性的基础；结果由 coordinating 节点归并。
why_en: Sharding spreads documents and their index structures across nodes so searches run in parallel and the coordinating node merges the results.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Index"] --> B["Primary shard"]
  B --> C["Replica 1"]
  B --> D["Replica 2"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引水平拆分出的一份数据与索引结构，1:1 对应一个 Lucene 索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shard is a horizontal slice of an index's data and index structures, mapping one-to-one to a Lucene index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收客户端请求、分发查询并合并结果的入口节点。

q_en: What core capability do shards give Elasticsearch?
optionExplanations: 分片把文档和索引结构水平拆到多台节点，搜索在相关分片上并行执行，由协调节点合并排序。
分片和数据加密是两回事，ES 不会因为分了片就自动加密存储。
有多个分片，每个索引依然需要 mapping，分片不能免掉这一步。
Elasticsearch 是最终一致，分片不会把它变成强一致系统。
optionExplanations_en: Sharding splits documents and index structure horizontally across nodes; search runs in parallel across the relevant shards and the coordinating node merges the results.
Sharding and data encryption are unrelated — having shards doesn't automatically encrypt storage.
Every index still needs mapping regardless of shard count — sharding doesn't remove that step.
Elasticsearch is eventually consistent; sharding doesn't turn it into a strongly consistent system.
scenario: 索引已经涨到 2TB、单机装不下，搜索还要求秒级返回，得靠某个机制横向摊开。
scenario_en: An index has grown to two terabytes, too big for one machine, yet search must still return within seconds.

q: 副本（replica）的两大用途是？
options: 对存储的数据做压缩处理，从而节省磁盘空间和成本
加快主分片自身的写入速度，同时减少段合并的次数
高可用备份 + 提高读吞吐（搜索在主副分片间负载均衡）
只是用来做离线备份归档，完全不参与实时的查询流量
options_en: Compressing stored data to save both disk space and cost
Speeding up the primary shard's own writes while reducing segment merges
High availability plus higher read throughput, load-balancing searches across primary and replica shards
Only for offline backup archiving, taking no part in live query traffic at all
why: replica 是分片的完整拷贝：既是故障备份，又能分担搜索流量——协调节点把查询分散到主分片和所有副本上。
why_en: Replicas provide high availability and extra read throughput, since the coordinating node balances searches across primary and replica shards.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分片的完整拷贝，用于故障恢复和分担查询流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replica is a full copy of a shard, used for failover and to share query load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引水平拆分出的一份数据与索引结构，1:1 对应一个 Lucene 索引。

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收客户端请求、分发查询并合并结果的入口节点。

q_en: What are the two main uses of replicas?
optionExplanations: 副本是完整数据拷贝，不做压缩处理，跟节省磁盘空间无关。
副本不参与主分片自身的写入路径优化，也不会减少段合并次数。
副本挂了有备份保高可用，协调节点还能把查询分散到主副本间提高读吞吐。
副本同时服务实时查询流量，不只是拿来做离线归档。
optionExplanations_en: A replica is a full copy of the data, not a compression trick — it has nothing to do with saving disk space.
Replicas don't speed up the primary shard's own write path or cut down merge counts.
Replicas back up the shard for high availability, and the coordinating node spreads search load across primary and replicas to boost read throughput.
Replicas also serve live query traffic — they aren't just an offline backup copy.
scenario: 索引的读 QPS 涨了 3 倍，同时要求单节点宕机既不丢数据也不中断搜索。
scenario_en: Read QPS on the index tripled, and a single node failure must neither lose data nor interrupt search.

scenario: 线上一个 primary shard 独立能扛住 X 的查询 TPS，运维给这个索引配置了 Y 个 replica。
q: 这时集群大致能扛住多少查询 TPS？
options: X + Y
还是 X
X 的平方
options_en: X plus Y
X times (Y plus one)
Still just X
X squared
why: TPS 是每秒查询数；1 个 primary shard + Y 个 replica shard 共有 Y+1 份可服务读的拷贝，所以搜索读容量近似 X*(Y+1)。这个数只用来估算查询吞吐，写入和复制开销不享受这层加成。
why_en: TPS means requests per second; one primary plus Y replicas gives Y+1 read-serving copies, so read capacity is roughly X times Y+1.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分片的完整拷贝，用于故障恢复和分担查询流量。

termDefinitions.meaning: 每份分片的主拷贝，写入先落到它，再复制到副本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A primary shard is the main copy of a shard; writes go there first and are then replicated.

termDefinitions.meaning: TPS 指每秒事务数；这里把一次搜索查询请求当作一个事务来估算吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TPS means transactions per second; here it approximates how many search requests the cluster can serve each second.

q_en: Roughly how much query TPS can this setup handle?
scenario_en: One primary shard can independently serve X query TPS, and operations configures Y replicas for this index.
optionExplanations: 把 TPS 和副本数直接相加，单位都对不上，也漏掉了每个副本是一份完整可读拷贝。
这把 primary 本身和 Y 个 replica 都算进读副本池；前提是查询能大致均匀分散。
只算主分片吞吐，等于假设副本完全不接查询流量，忽视了 replica 的读扩展作用。
副本只增加可服务读的拷贝数，不会让吞吐变成平方增长；这里把线性关系算错了。
optionExplanations_en: Adding TPS to a replica count mixes units and misses that each replica is a full readable copy.
This counts the primary plus Y replicas in the read pool, assuming queries spread roughly evenly.
Counting only the primary assumes replicas serve no query traffic, which ignores their read-scaling role.
Replicas add readable copies; they do not make throughput grow quadratically.

q: Lucene 的 segment 最核心的性质是？
options: 可以就地修改
只存在于内存里
不可变（immutable）的已索引数据容器
每个文档单独一个 segment
options_en: It can be modified in place
It only exists in memory
An immutable container of indexed data
Every document gets its own segment
why: segment 是搜索引擎的基本单元，且一旦写成就不可变——增删改都是靠新 segment、软删除和合并来间接实现的。
why_en: A segment is an immutable container of indexed data, and all updates happen through new segments, soft deletes, and merges.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["New docs"] --> B["New segment"]
  B --> C["Immutable files"]
  C --> D["Merge later"]

termDefinitions.meaning: Lucene 索引里不可变的已索引数据容器，是写入和合并的基本单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A segment is an immutable container of indexed data, the basic unit of writes and merges in Lucene.

q_en: What is the most important property of a Lucene segment?
optionExplanations: 这里正好说反了 segment 最核心的性质——它写成后就不可变。
segment 会落盘持久化，不是只存在于内存里。
segment 是一旦写成就不可变的已索引数据容器，增删改都靠新 segment 间接实现。
segment 是批量构建的，不是每个文档单独一个。
optionExplanations_en: This has it exactly backwards — the whole point of a segment is that it's immutable once written.
Segments get flushed to disk; they don't live only in memory.
A segment is an immutable, already-indexed data container once written — inserts, deletes, and updates all happen indirectly through new segments.
Segments are built in batches, not created one per document.
scenario: Lucene 要同时扛住高写入吞吐和安全缓存，段的设计上因此做了一个关键取舍。
scenario_en: Lucene must sustain high write throughput and safe caching at once, which drives one key property of its segments.

q: 插入一个新文档时，Lucene 实际做了什么？
options: 攒批：文档进待写批次，凑够一批建成新 segment 刷盘
把新文档直接插进已有 segment 的中间位置并改写它
每插入一条文档就重写一遍整个索引
文档只写进内存，永远不会刷到磁盘
options_en: Batch first: documents accumulate, then a full batch is built into a new segment and flushed to disk
Insert the new document directly into the middle of an existing segment and rewrite it
Rewrite the entire index for every single document inserted
Write the document only to memory and never flush it to disk
why: 写入是批量构建新 segment 的过程，不修改既有 segment——这是不可变设计下高写入吞吐的来源。
why_en: Inserts are batched into new segments that get flushed to disk, never modifying existing segments.

termDefinitions.meaning: Lucene 索引里不可变的已索引数据容器，是写入和合并的基本单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A segment is an immutable container of indexed data, the basic unit of writes and merges in Lucene.

q_en: What does Lucene actually do when inserting a new document?
optionExplanations: 新文档先进待写批次，攒够一批后构建成一个新 segment 刷到磁盘。
segment 一旦写成就不再被修改，不能把新文档插进已有 segment 中间。
写入只影响新构建的 segment，不会碰既有索引的全量重写。
数据最终会被刷到磁盘，不是永远只留在内存里。
optionExplanations_en: New documents first queue up in a pending batch, and once enough accumulate they get built into a brand-new segment flushed to disk.
A segment can't be modified once written, so a new document can't be inserted into the middle of an existing one.
A write only produces a new segment — it never rewrites the whole existing index.
The data does eventually get flushed to disk — it doesn't stay in memory forever.
scenario: 日志系统每秒写入 5 万条文档，而 Lucene 的 segment 一旦写成就不可变。
scenario_en: A logging system indexes fifty thousand documents per second while Lucene segments are immutable once written.

q: segment 数量太多时，Lucene 怎么处理？
options: 为了腾出空间，自动把最老的几个 segment 直接删掉
在合并完成之前直接拒绝任何新的写入请求
把多余的 segment 打包上传到远端对象存储归档
merge：把多个 segment 合并成一个并移除旧的
options_en: Automatically delete the oldest segments outright to free up space
Reject any new write requests until the merge finishes
Package the excess segments and upload them to remote object storage for archiving
Merge: combine several segments into one and drop the old ones
why: 段合并把碎片化的 segment 归并成大 segment，顺带物理清理软删除的数据。
why_en: Lucene merges numerous small segments into a new larger one and removes the old segments.

termDefinitions.meaning: Lucene 索引里不可变的已索引数据容器，是写入和合并的基本单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A segment is an immutable container of indexed data, the basic unit of writes and merges in Lucene.

q_en: What does Lucene do when there are too many segments?
optionExplanations: 合并不会把最老的数据直接删掉，它只是重新组织数据。
segment 太多会拖慢查询，但不会导致 Lucene 拒绝新的写入请求。
段合并是本地磁盘上的操作，不涉及上传到远端对象存储。
merge 把多个 segment 合并成一个新的更大 segment，并顺带移除旧的、清理软删除的数据。
optionExplanations_en: Merging doesn't drop the oldest data outright — it just reorganizes it.
Too many segments slows queries, but it doesn't make Lucene reject new writes.
Segment merging is a local-disk operation, not an upload to remote object storage.
A merge folds several segments into one larger new segment, removing the old ones and cleaning up soft-deleted data along the way.
scenario: 高频写入让一个分片攒出上千个小 segment，每次查询都要挨个扫，延迟明显变差。
scenario_en: Heavy writes leave a shard with thousands of tiny segments that every query must scan, and latency has gotten noticeably worse.

q: segment 不可变，删除文档是怎么实现的？
options: 就地重写那个 segment 文件的内容，把这条记录去掉
维护「已删除 ID 集合」软删除，merge 时才物理清理
删除请求一到就立即把数据从磁盘上物理抹除干净
把被删除的文档统一挪到一个专门的回收站索引里保存
options_en: Rewrite that segment file's content in place to drop the record
Maintain a deleted-id set as a soft delete; the data is only physically removed at merge time
Physically erase the data from disk the instant the delete request arrives
Move deleted documents into a dedicated trash index for safekeeping
why: 每个 segment 带一个删除标记集合；被删文档查询时被跳过但数据还在，直到段合并时才物理清除。删除因此非常快。
why_en: Deletes are soft: the segment marks the document as deleted and hides it from queries, and merges later physically remove it.

termDefinitions.meaning: Lucene 索引里不可变的已索引数据容器，是写入和合并的基本单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A segment is an immutable container of indexed data, the basic unit of writes and merges in Lucene.

q_en: If segments are immutable, how is a document delete implemented?
optionExplanations: segment 不可变，不会被就地重写去掉一条记录。
维护一份「已删除 ID」集合做软删除：查询时跳过它，数据本体保留到 merge 才真正清掉。
物理数据其实还留在原地，直到 merge 才被清除，不是删除请求一到就抹除。
Elasticsearch 没有专门的回收站索引这种设计。
optionExplanations_en: Segments are immutable, so a record never gets removed by rewriting the file in place.
It keeps a set of deleted IDs as a soft-delete marker — queries skip that document, but the data stays on disk until a merge actually clears it.
The physical data actually stays put until a merge runs — it isn't wiped the instant a delete request arrives.
There's no dedicated 'recycle bin' index in Elasticsearch's design.
scenario: 用户删掉一条评论，但 segment 不可变、磁盘数据不能就地改，删除只能另想办法。
scenario_en: A user deletes a review, but segments are immutable and the on-disk data cannot be edited in place, so delete needs another route.

q: 为什么在 Elasticsearch 里「更新」比「插入」性能更差？
options: 更新操作需要给整个集群加上一把全局互斥锁才能进行写入操作
更新操作必须同步等待数据真正刷盘落地完成之后才能返回结果
更新 = 软删旧文档 + 插入新文档，簿记要到 merge 才清
一次更新会让集群里全部的查询缓存瞬间统统失效并重新构建
options_en: An update requires taking a global mutex lock across the whole cluster before it can proceed
An update must synchronously wait for the data to actually flush and land on disk before it can return
An update is a soft delete plus a new insert, and the bookkeeping isn't cleared until a merge
A single update instantly invalidates and forces a rebuild of every query cache in the cluster
why: 更新不改 segment，而是软删 + 重插，代价高于纯插入；这正是 ES 不适合「频繁更新的数据」的底层原因。
why_en: An update soft-deletes the old document and inserts a new one, adding bookkeeping overhead that lingers until segments merge, which is why Elasticsearch dislikes rapidly updating data.

termDefinitions.meaning: Lucene 索引里不可变的已索引数据容器，是写入和合并的基本单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A segment is an immutable container of indexed data, the basic unit of writes and merges in Lucene.

q_en: Why are updates slower than inserts in Elasticsearch?
optionExplanations: 更新路径不涉及给整个集群加全局互斥锁。
刷盘策略对插入和更新是一致的，不是更新独有的额外负担。
更新 = 软删旧文档 + 插入新文档，多出一份簿记，在 merge 清理前一直拖着性能。
这里说的是索引层机制，不会让全部查询缓存瞬间失效重建。
optionExplanations_en: The update path doesn't involve taking a global cluster-wide lock.
Flush policy is the same for inserts and updates — it isn't an update-specific tax.
An update is really a soft-delete of the old document plus an insert of a new one, adding bookkeeping that drags on performance until the next merge cleans it up.
This is an index-layer mechanism, not something that invalidates and rebuilds every query cache at once.
scenario: 商品价格每分钟都在变，团队想直接更新 ES 文档的 price 字段，先要算清更新的代价。
scenario_en: Product prices change every minute and the team wants to update the price field in Elasticsearch directly, so the cost of an update matters.

q: 不可变 segment 带来哪些好处？（多选）
options: 新文档直接进新 segment，写入吞吐高
可以放心缓存和更高效压缩，无一致性顾虑
读操作不怕数据中途被改，并发和崩溃恢复都更简单
更新可以就地修改文档，最高效
options_en: New documents go straight into new segments for high write throughput
Data can be safely cached and compressed with no consistency worries
Reads never worry about data changing mid-query, simplifying concurrency and crash recovery
Updates can modify documents in place for maximum efficiency
why: 不可变换来：快写入、安全缓存、优化压缩、简化并发、易恢复、更快搜索。代价是要周期性 merge，且清理前占用额外存储。
why_en: Immutability speeds writes, enables safe caching and better compression, and simplifies concurrency and recovery, at the cost of periodic merges.

termDefinitions.meaning: Lucene 索引里不可变的已索引数据容器，是写入和合并的基本单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A segment is an immutable container of indexed data, the basic unit of writes and merges in Lucene.

q_en: Which benefits come from immutable segments? (Select all that apply.)
optionExplanations: 新文档直接进新 segment，不用碰旧数据，写入吞吐因此更高。
数据写成后不会再变，缓存和压缩都能放心做，不用担心失效一致性问题。
读不用处理数据被并发改写的情况，崩溃恢复的逻辑也更简单。
这里正好和不可变性矛盾——segment 恰恰不支持就地修改文档。
optionExplanations_en: New documents land straight in a fresh segment without touching old ones, which is why write throughput stays high.
Once data is written it never changes again, so caching and compression can proceed without worrying about invalidation.
Reads never have to handle data being modified underneath them, which also makes crash recovery simpler.
This directly contradicts immutability — segments specifically don't support editing a document in place.
scenario: 日志集群每秒写入十万条、同时靠缓存扛读，段一旦写成就不再被修改。
scenario_en: A logging cluster indexes a hundred thousand documents a second and leans on caching for reads, with segments never modified once written.

q: 不可变 segment 设计的主要代价是？
options: 需要周期性段合并，且清理完成前暂时占用更多存储
所有的读请求都会因此明显变慢
这套设计导致完全没法做全文搜索
这套设计导致索引没办法再配置副本
options_en: Periodic segment merging is required, with temporarily higher storage until cleanup finishes
Every read request would become noticeably slower because of this
This design makes full-text search completely impossible
This design makes it impossible to configure replicas for the index
why: 软删除的数据在 merge 前一直占着空间、拖着查询，merge 本身也消耗 I/O 和 CPU——这是拿空间和后台工作换读写性能。
why_en: The price of immutability is periodic segment merging and temporarily higher storage until deleted data is cleaned up.

termDefinitions.meaning: Lucene 索引里不可变的已索引数据容器，是写入和合并的基本单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A segment is an immutable container of indexed data, the basic unit of writes and merges in Lucene.

q_en: What is the main cost of immutable segments?
optionExplanations: 需要周期性段合并，且在清理完成前，软删数据会暂时多占存储空间。
不可变设计整体上是为了让读更快更简单，不是让读请求变慢。
不可变性不影响全文搜索这个能力本身，两者没有冲突。
副本机制是独立配置，跟 segment 是否可变没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: It needs periodic segment merges, and until cleanup finishes, soft-deleted data temporarily takes up extra storage.
Immutability is meant to make reads faster and simpler overall — it doesn't slow requests down.
Immutability doesn't take away full-text search capability itself — the two aren't in conflict.
Replica configuration is independent of whether segments are mutable.
scenario: 索引里 30% 的文档已被软删除，磁盘用量远高于实际数据，后台还在跑合并。
scenario_en: Thirty percent of documents in the index are soft-deleted, disk usage far exceeds the live data, and merges keep running in the background.

q: 倒排索引（inverted index）是什么？它为什么让关键词搜索快？
options: 把全部文档按 ID 从小到大排好序，存成一份顺序列表
「词 → 含该词的文档列表」的映射，把 O(n) 扫描变查表
对文档的原始内容整体做一次 gzip 压缩后存起来
把出现过的所有词，都存进一棵普通的平衡二叉树里
options_en: A list of all documents sorted by id from smallest to largest, stored in order
A mapping from term to the documents containing it, turning an O(n) scan into a table lookup
A single gzip compression pass run over the raw document content
Storing every term that ever appeared in an ordinary balanced binary tree
why: 为每个唯一词记录它出现在哪些文档里——找「含 lazy 的书」不再扫 10 亿本书，直接查表。这是「复制数据并按检索方式重排」的经典应用。
why_en: An inverted index maps each term to the documents containing it, turning a linear scan into a near constant-time lookup.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["term bill"] --> B["doc 1"]
  A --> C["doc 7"]
  D["term nye"] --> C
  D --> E["doc 9"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 从词到包含该词的文档列表的映射，让关键词查找接近 O(1)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each term to the documents containing it, turning search into a near constant-time lookup.

q_en: What is an inverted index, and why does it make keyword search fast?
optionExplanations: 按 ID 排好序的一份列表不能直接支持按关键词查找。
从「词→含该词的文档列表」的映射入手，把全量扫描变成近似 O(1) 的直接查表。
gzip 压缩解决的是存储体积问题，不解决查找效率问题。
平衡二叉树擅长范围顺序查询，不是词到文档集合的映射结构。
optionExplanations_en: A list simply sorted by document ID can't directly support keyword lookup.
It maps each word to the list of documents containing it, turning a full scan into an almost O(1) table lookup.
gzip compression solves a storage-size problem, not a lookup-efficiency problem.
A balanced binary tree is good at ordered range queries, not at mapping a word to its set of documents.
scenario: 书库有 10 亿本书，用户搜「lazy」要在毫秒内拿到所有含这个词的书。
scenario_en: A catalog holds a billion books, and a search for the word lazy must return every book containing it within milliseconds.

q: doc values 是什么结构？解决什么问题？
options: 写入的同时自动生成一份文档的备份副本存起来
专门缓存最近几次查询结果、加速重复查询的查询缓存
在倒排索引基础上做进一步压缩得到的一个压缩版本
某字段跨全段文档的列式连续存储，排序只读这一列
options_en: A backup copy of the document automatically generated alongside the write itself
A dedicated query cache that speeds up repeated queries by storing recent results
A further-compressed version built on top of the inverted index
A columnar contiguous store of one field across a whole segment, so a sort reads only that column
why: 行式存储取单列也要读整行；doc values 像 Spark/Redshift 一样按列连续存储单字段，排序聚合时只读需要的那一列。
why_en: Doc values store one field for all documents in a columnar contiguous layout, so sorting and aggregations read only that column instead of whole rows.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按字段列式连续存储的结构，支撑排序和聚合而不必读整行文档。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Doc values store one field for all documents in a columnar layout so sorting and aggregation avoid reading whole rows.

q_en: What structure are doc values, and what problem do they solve?
optionExplanations: doc values 不是写入时自动生成的备份副本，它是查询期要用的结构。
它不是缓存最近查询结果的东西，而是持久化落盘的列式数据。
它和倒排索引是两个独立结构，不是在倒排基础上再压缩出来的版本。
它把某个字段跨全段文档按列连续存储，排序聚合时只读这一列，不必读整行文档。
optionExplanations_en: doc values aren't an automatic backup copy generated at write time — it's a structure used during queries.
It isn't a cache of recent query results, it's persisted, on-disk columnar data.
It's a separate structure from the inverted index, not a further-compressed version built on top of it.
It stores one field contiguously by column across a whole segment, so sorting or aggregating only reads that column instead of the entire row.
scenario: 一次搜索命中 50 万商品要按 price 排序，行式读回整份文档太浪费 I/O。
scenario_en: A search matches half a million products that must be sorted by price, and reading whole documents row-wise wastes far too much I/O.

q: 倒排索引与 doc values 在一次「搜索 + 按价格排序」里的分工是？
options: 倒排索引找出匹配文档，doc values 提供 price 列做排序
倒排索引和 doc values 其实都是用来找文档的
反过来，doc values 负责找文档，倒排索引负责排序
倒排索引只在写入文档时用到，查询时用不上
options_en: The inverted index finds the matching documents while doc values supply the price column for sorting
Both the inverted index and doc values are actually used to find documents
The reverse: doc values find documents and the inverted index does the sorting
The inverted index is only touched during writes and plays no role at query time
tradeoff: 倒排索引找文档（行方向）vs doc values 排序聚合（列方向）
why: token → 文档靠倒排索引；文档 → 排序字段值靠 doc values。一个管「找到谁」，一个管「按什么排」。
why_en: The inverted index finds which documents match, and doc values supply the field values needed to sort those matches.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从词到包含该词的文档列表的映射，让关键词查找接近 O(1)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each term to the documents containing it, turning search into a near constant-time lookup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按字段列式连续存储的结构，支撑排序和聚合而不必读整行文档。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Doc values store one field for all documents in a columnar layout so sorting and aggregation avoid reading whole rows.

q_en: How do the inverted index and doc values split work in search plus price sorting?
optionExplanations: 关键词先靠倒排索引找出候选文档，doc values 再给这些文档的排序字段值——两步各管一段。
只在不需要排序聚合的纯词项查询时，doc values 可能才不参与。
doc values 是列式取值结构，负责不了从 token 找文档这一步。
倒排索引在查询的 query 阶段同样要用，不是只在写入时起作用。
optionExplanations_en: Keywords first find candidate documents through the inverted index, then doc values supply the sort field values for those documents — two separate steps.
doc values might sit out only for a pure term-match query that needs no sorting or aggregation at all.
doc values is a columnar lookup structure — it can't do the token-to-document step.
The inverted index gets used during the query stage too, not only while writing.
scenario: 一次「标题匹配关键词 + 按 price 升序」的查询，要说清哪一步用哪个结构。
scenario_en: For a query that matches a keyword in the title and sorts by ascending price, you must say which structure does which step.

q: coordinating 节点上的查询规划器（query planner）靠什么决定执行方式？
options: 每次都在几种候选执行计划里完全随机挑选一个来执行
永远严格按照查询语句里写下来的先后顺序依次执行
统计信息：字段类型、词频、文档长度，据此选执行顺序
执行方式的选择只取决于集群里一共有多少个节点
options_en: Randomly picking one of several candidate execution plans completely at random each time
Always strictly executing step by step in the exact order the query was written in
Statistics — field types, term frequencies, document lengths — used to pick the execution order
The choice of execution style depends only on how many nodes the cluster happens to have
why: 规划器基于统计选择用哪个索引、按什么顺序执行、如何合并多节点结果；「数据依赖」的自适应正是数据库系统强大的原因。
why_en: The query planner uses statistics on fields, term popularity, and document lengths to pick the cheapest execution order dynamically.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 coordinating 节点上依据统计信息选择最优执行方式的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The query planner is the component on the coordinating node that uses statistics to choose the cheapest execution plan.

q_en: What does the query planner on a coordinating node use to choose an execution plan?
optionExplanations: 真要随机挑，性能会完全不可预测，跟实际表现不符。
严格按语句写下的顺序执行等于忽视统计信息，会错失很大的优化空间。
规划器基于字段类型、热门关键词、文档长度等统计信息，动态选出最省时间的执行顺序。
节点数只是集群拓扑信息，不是查询代价估算依赖的关键统计量。
optionExplanations_en: If it really picked at random, performance would be unpredictable, which doesn't match reality.
Strictly following the order written in the query would ignore statistics and miss a lot of optimization headroom.
The planner uses statistics like field type, popular terms, and document length to dynamically pick the fastest execution order.
Node count is just cluster topology, not a key statistic for estimating query cost.
scenario: 一次 bool 查询里既有高频词 match 又有 range 过滤，执行顺序不同耗时差几个数量级。
scenario_en: A bool query mixes a high-frequency term match with a range filter, and execution order changes the cost by orders of magnitude.

q: 搜索 "bill nye"：倒排索引里 "bill" 有几百万条、"nye" 只有几百条。高效的执行方式是？
options: 先把 "bill" 那几百万条候选文档全部扫一遍再处理
从 "nye" 的几百条小集合入手做交集验证短语
干脆放弃倒排索引带来的优势，直接全表扫描所有文档
把两个词各自的候选集都并行全量展开出来，再求交集
options_en: Scan through all of bill's millions of candidate documents first and process from there
Start from nye's few hundred postings and intersect to verify the phrase
Give up the inverted index's advantage entirely and just full-scan every document
Fully expand each term's own candidate set in parallel and then intersect them
why: 不同执行顺序性能差几个数量级；从稀有词的小结果集出发再验证短语，是规划器靠词频统计做的典型优化。
why_en: Starting from the rare term's few hundred postings and intersecting is orders of magnitude cheaper than expanding the common term's millions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从词到包含该词的文档列表的映射，让关键词查找接近 O(1)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each term to the documents containing it, turning search into a near constant-time lookup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 coordinating 节点上依据统计信息选择最优执行方式的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The query planner is the component on the coordinating node that uses statistics to choose the cheapest execution plan.

q_en: For the search "bill nye", with millions of "bill" hits and hundreds of "nye" hits, what is efficient?
optionExplanations: 先碰几百万条候选，后续交集运算的基数被拉得很高，代价最大。
从 "nye" 的几百条小集合入手做验证，避免一上来就处理几百万条的大集合。
全表扫描是最慢的兜底方式，规划器不会主动放弃索引优势去选它。
两边都并行全量展开，等于百万级集合的开销一分没省。
optionExplanations_en: Starting from the few-million-document set makes every downstream intersection operate on a huge base — the most expensive path.
Starting from "nye"'s small few-hundred set and verifying against it avoids ever touching the million-document set.
A full scan is the slowest fallback — the planner wouldn't deliberately give up the index's advantage for it.
Expanding both terms in full in parallel still pays the full cost of the million-row set — nothing is saved.
scenario: 短语搜索 "bill nye" 要求毫秒级返回，而两个词的候选集大小差了四个数量级。
scenario_en: A phrase search for "bill nye" must return in milliseconds, yet the two terms differ in posting-list size by four orders of magnitude.

q: 面试中 Elasticsearch 最常见的接入方式是？
options: 通过 CDC 挂在权威数据库（Postgres/DynamoDB）旁做搜索层
把 Elasticsearch 当成系统里唯一的持久化数据库长期使用
用 Elasticsearch 直接替换掉 Kafka 这一类消息队列系统
仅仅把 Elasticsearch 当成前端页面渲染用的缓存层而已
options_en: Attached as a search layer via CDC next to an authoritative store like Postgres or DynamoDB
Used long-term as the system's sole persistent database
Used as a direct replacement for an entire message queue system like Kafka
Used merely as a cache layer for rendering front-end pages, nothing more
why: 权威数据留在主库，变更通过 CDC 流进 Elasticsearch 供搜索——Elasticsearch 是「衍生数据」层，不是 source of truth。
why_en: In interviews Elasticsearch is usually attached via change data capture to an authoritative store like Postgres or DynamoDB.

termDefinitions.meaning: 持续捕获权威数据库变更并同步到下游系统的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Change data capture continuously streams changes from an authoritative database to downstream systems.

q_en: What is the most common way to connect Elasticsearch in a system-design interview?
optionExplanations: 权威数据留在主库，靠 CDC 把变更流实时同步进它做搜索层，这是最稳妥的接入方式。
ES 的持久性历史上不够稳固，不该把它当成系统唯一的持久化数据库。
ES 不提供消息队列那种持久投递语义，替代不了 Kafka 这类系统。
它确实能加速查询，但角色是搜索引擎，不只是给前端渲染用的缓存层。
optionExplanations_en: Authoritative data stays in the primary store, and CDC streams changes into it in real time as the search layer — the steadiest way to wire it in.
Elasticsearch's durability has historically been shaky, so it shouldn't be the system's sole persistent database.
Elasticsearch doesn't offer the durable delivery guarantees of a message queue — it can't replace something like Kafka.
It does speed up queries, but its role is a search engine, not just a rendering cache for the frontend.
scenario: 面试里要给订单系统加全文搜索，权威订单数据已经在 Postgres 里且绝不能丢。
scenario_en: In an interview you add full-text search to an order system whose authoritative data already lives in Postgres and cannot be lost.

q: 把 Elasticsearch 当主数据库（唯一持久存储）的问题是？
options: 主要问题只是查询响应速度太慢
它是搜索引擎不是数据库：历史上有一致性与持久性问题，需要持久的数据应放在别处
Elasticsearch 根本没办法存储 JSON 格式的数据
主要问题在于它的存储成本太贵
options_en: The main issue is simply that query response would be too slow
It is a search engine, not a database, with a history of consistency and durability issues, so data that must persist belongs elsewhere
Elasticsearch simply has no way to store JSON-formatted data
The main issue is that its storage cost would be too high
why: Elasticsearch 是搜索引擎，不是唯一 source of truth；它为搜索/分析优化，历史上也踩过一致性和持久性坑。不能丢的数据放 Postgres/DynamoDB 这类主库，再同步进它。
why_en: Use Elasticsearch as a search index, not the only source of truth, because it is optimized for search rather than transactional durability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 Lucene 的分布式搜索与分析引擎，常作为主库之外的搜索索引层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is a distributed search and analytics engine built on Lucene, often used as a search index beside a primary database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统里被当作权威事实的存储；其他索引或缓存都应能从它重建。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A source of truth is the authoritative store that other indexes or caches can be rebuilt from.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种键值结构的数据格式，Elasticsearch 文档通常就是 JSON 对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: JSON means JavaScript Object Notation, a key-value data format commonly used for Elasticsearch documents.

termDefinitions.meaning: 另一个历史上曾有持久性与一致性争议的文档数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CouchDB is another document database with a historical reputation for consistency and durability issues.

q_en: What is wrong with using Elasticsearch as the only primary database?
optionExplanations: 查询速度通常是它的强项；把它当唯一主库的风险在持久性和一致性。
这条是在划清角色边界：权威存储要承诺事务和持久化，搜索层可以从主库重建。
它的文档本来就是 JSON；问题不是能不能存，而是能不能做唯一权威存储。
存储成本可能要算，但它不是这里的主风险；更要紧的是数据丢失或不一致。
optionExplanations_en: Query speed is usually Elasticsearch's strength; the risk of making it the only primary store is durability and consistency.
This draws the role boundary: Elasticsearch serves search, while authoritative data stays in a real primary database.
Elasticsearch documents are already JSON; the issue is authority, not whether JSON can be stored.
Storage cost can matter, but it is not the main risk here; data loss or inconsistency is.
scenario: 创业团队想少维护一套系统，把订单数据只存在 Elasticsearch 里，订单绝不能丢。
scenario_en: A startup wants to run one less system and store orders only in Elasticsearch, but orders absolutely cannot be lost.

scenario: 社交产品想在搜索结果里展示帖子的点赞数和曝光数，这些计数每秒都在变，有人提议直接在 ES 文档里加字段实时更新。
q: 更合理的做法是？
options: 照做，每次用户点赞都实时更新一次 Elasticsearch 文档
改成每隔一小时，把整个索引从头到尾全量重建一次
计数放权威存储/缓存，批量异步刷进 ES 或查询时再取
干脆在搜索结果页面里，把这些计数字段全部隐藏不展示
options_en: Do it anyway, updating the Elasticsearch document in real time on every single like
Switch to rebuilding the entire index from scratch, start to finish, once every hour
Keep counters in an authoritative store or cache and batch-flush them into Elasticsearch, or fetch them at query time
Simply hide these count fields entirely and stop showing them on the results page
tradeoff: 高频写入的实时性 vs Elasticsearch 更新（软删+重插）的代价
why: Elasticsearch 面向读多写少：更新 = 软删+重插，高频计数更新会让它挣扎。写缓冲/批量同步或读时补充计数才是对的。
why_en: Elasticsearch is built for read-heavy workloads, so rapidly changing counters should be buffered and batched into it rather than written per event.
whenOtherWins: 字段更新频率低（如商品标题偶尔改）时，直接更新 Elasticsearch 文档完全没问题。

termDefinitions.meaning: Lucene 索引里不可变的已索引数据容器，是写入和合并的基本单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A segment is an immutable container of indexed data, the basic unit of writes and merges in Lucene.

q_en: What is the more reasonable design?
scenario_en: A social product wants likes and impression counts in search results; those counters change every second, and someone suggests updating the ES document on every event.
optionExplanations: 计数更新频率很低、能容忍短暂旧值时可以直接写 ES；这里是每秒都变，每次点赞都触发软删+重插，会拖垮集群。
只有离线批处理、能接受长时间旧数据时才适合整索引重建；一小时一次实时性太差。
计数放权威存储/缓存，写缓冲批量异步刷进 ES，或查询时再补充计数——把高频写路径和搜索索引解耦。
产品能接受不展示计数时才算需求层的取舍；这里是回避问题，不是方案。
optionExplanations_en: Direct real-time writes are fine when counters change rarely and staleness is tolerable — here they change every second, so each like triggers a soft-delete-plus-reinsert that would bog the cluster down.
A full index rebuild only fits offline batch work that can tolerate long staleness — once an hour is far too stale here.
Keep counts in an authoritative store or cache and flush them into Elasticsearch in async batches (or fetch them at query time) — decoupling the hot write path from the search index.
Hiding the counters is only a legitimate product tradeoff if the business accepts it — here it just avoids the problem instead of solving it.

q: 使用 Elasticsearch 时必须向面试官承认的一致性事实是？
options: 搜索结果是最终一致的，会读到过期数据，容忍不了就换方案
Elasticsearch 对跨文档操作提供可串行化事务保证
Elasticsearch 每次写入都是同步落盘的强一致操作
主分片和副本之间的数据永远保持瞬时一致
options_en: Search results are eventually consistent and can be stale, so an intolerant use case needs another approach
Elasticsearch provides serializable transaction guarantees across documents
Every Elasticsearch write is a synchronously flushed, strongly consistent operation
Data between the primary shard and its replicas is always instantaneously in sync
why: 从写入到可搜索有延迟，CDC 同步又加一层滞后——结果「必然」stale。设计时要明说这一点并确认业务能容忍。
why_en: Elasticsearch is eventually consistent, so search results will be stale, sometimes significantly, and the design must tolerate that.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入后不保证立刻可见，短暂之后各副本才收敛到一致状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency means a write is not guaranteed to be immediately visible, only visible after some delay.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分片的完整拷贝，用于故障恢复和分担查询流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replica is a full copy of a shard, used for failover and to share query load.

q_en: What consistency fact must you acknowledge when using Elasticsearch?
optionExplanations: 结果必然是最终一致的，会读到过期数据，有时滞后还很明显——不能容忍就得换方案。
Elasticsearch 不提供跨文档的可串行化事务保证。
写入到可搜索之间存在刷新延迟，不是同步落盘的强一致操作。
主副本之间的同步也有延迟窗口，不是瞬时一致。
optionExplanations_en: Results are necessarily eventually consistent — you can read stale data, sometimes noticeably delayed, and if the business can't tolerate that you need a different approach.
Elasticsearch doesn't offer serializable transactions across documents.
There's a refresh delay between writing and being searchable — it isn't a synchronous, strongly consistent write.
Replica sync also has a delay window — it isn't instantaneously consistent either.
scenario: 用户改完昵称立刻搜自己：主库已更新，ES 靠 CDC 同步，产品问「能保证搜到吗」。
scenario_en: A user renames themselves and immediately searches for it: the primary store is updated but Elasticsearch syncs via CDC.

q: 在 Elasticsearch 里建模数据的指导原则是？
options: 像关系型数据库一样，严格遵守三范式，尽量避免出现任何数据冗余
把数据拆分到多个不同的索引里，查询时再手动跨索引做 join 关联
每个文档只放一个字段，字段和字段之间各自单独建一份文档存储
尽量反范式化：目标是 1-2 个查询拿到结果，写入侧多做转换
options_en: Strictly follow third normal form like a relational database, avoiding any data redundancy at all costs
Split data across many different indices and manually join across them at query time
Put only one field per document, with every field living in its own separate document
Denormalize aggressively — the goal is one or two queries per request, with more work on the write side
why: Elasticsearch 没有 join，把数据按查询模式摊平（denormalize），写入时做转换，换取查询侧的高效。
why_en: Denormalize aggressively since Elasticsearch is not relational, aiming to answer each request with one or two queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为查询效率牺牲数据冗余，把关联数据摊平进同一文档。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization trades data redundancy for query efficiency by flattening related data into one document.

q_en: What is the guiding rule for modeling data in Elasticsearch?
optionExplanations: 严格三范式会迫使查询侧做大量关联，而 ES 并不擅长这个。
ES 没有原生 join，跨索引关联要靠应用层自己拼，这个前提假设不成立。
一个字段一个文档会让最基本的查询都要多次往返，粒度切得太碎。

q_en: What is the reasonable first step?
scenario_en: An internal tool needs a search box over fewer than 100k records that rarely change.

optionExplanations_en: A dedicated cluster is worth deploying once search becomes the critical path and the primary database clearly can't keep up — for under 100k rarely-changing records, that's over-engineering.
When the data is small, rarely changes, and search needs are simple, start with the primary database's own query or full-text features and upgrade only if that stops being enough.
The full CDC pipeline earns its keep when you need a reliable change stream and an independent search cluster — at this scale the sync plumbing and ops cost aren't worth it.
Rolling your own inverted index only makes sense for teaching or very unusual constraints — normal cases should just use an existing implementation.

scenario: 商品、帖子或店铺的权威数据存在主库里，CDC 把变更同步到 Elasticsearch，ES 只负责搜索索引。
q: Elasticsearch 与底层权威数据的同步失败，会导致什么？如何应对？
options: Elasticsearch 会自动知道哪里漂移，并自己回源修复
同步失败只会稍微拖慢一点点写入速度，完全不影响查询结果的正确性
搜索索引与 source of truth 发生 drift，要监控并对账重建
同步只要一失败，整个集群就会立刻直接宕机彻底崩溃，谁都没法恢复
options_en: Elasticsearch automatically knows which records drifted and repairs itself from the source
A sync failure only slows writes down a little and does not affect the correctness of query results at all
The search index drifts from the source of truth, so you need sync monitoring plus reconciliation or reindexing
The instant sync fails, the entire cluster crashes hard and completely, with no way to recover
why: drift 是 ES 索引和主库真相不一致：搜索可能漏新数据、显示旧数据或搜到已删除数据。修复依赖真相源或可 replay 的变更日志，而不是 ES 自己凭空恢复。
why_en: Drift means the Elasticsearch index no longer matches the source of truth; repair depends on the primary store or replayable change log, not Elasticsearch magically healing itself.
whenOtherWins: 如果权威数据或可重放事件日志也丢了，就不能可靠重建 ES；只能从备份、审计日志或业务补录里恢复。

q_en: What happens if Elasticsearch falls out of sync with the source of truth, and how do you handle it?
scenario_en: Products, posts, or stores live in a primary database; CDC syncs changes into Elasticsearch, which is only the search index.
optionExplanations: ES 不知道主库最新状态，不会自己发现漂移并回源修复，这个说法夸大了它的能力。
影响不只是拖慢写入速度那么轻，用户可能搜不到新数据、看到旧数据甚至搜到已删数据。
搜索索引会和 source of truth 产生 drift，要靠监控发现、再从真相源（重建或 CDC/Kafka replay）对账修复。
同步失败不会让整个集群立刻宕机，只是索引内容变得不可信，服务仍在跑。
optionExplanations_en: Elasticsearch doesn't know the primary's latest state and won't self-detect drift and heal itself — that overstates what it can do.
The impact isn't just a minor write-speed hit — users can miss new data, see stale data, or even find results that were already deleted.
The search index drifts away from the source of truth; you need monitoring to catch it and a reconcile/rebuild from the true source (or CDC/Kafka replay) to fix it.
Sync failures don't crash the whole cluster outright — the service keeps running, it's just the index contents that become untrustworthy.

data 节点专注存储与本地搜索，coordinating 节点专注解析、分发与合并

The reverse: coordinating nodes store data and data nodes handle routing
Data nodes focus on storage and local search execution while coordinating nodes parse, route, and merge
Data nodes only handle write requests and take no part in search execution

why: 存储与查询编排分离让两类节点可按各自瓶颈独立扩展和调优，是 Elasticsearch 架构的一条核心设计经验。
why_en: Data nodes focus on storage and local search execution while coordinating nodes parse, route, and merge, letting each be optimized independently.

Storage bottlenecks and query-orchestration bottlenecks are usually different, so splitting them across two node types lets each scale and tune independently.

scenario: 日志检索用 search_after 顺序翻几十万条，很多文档的 timestamp 撞在同一毫秒；工程师的 sort 只写了 [timestamp desc]，没带 _id 之类唯一 tie-breaker。
q: 少了唯一 tie-breaker，深翻页会怎么坏掉？
options: 同 timestamp 的文档没有稳定顺序，游标切在这批中间，部分文档重复、部分被漏
Elasticsearch 直接拒绝该请求，强制你先补一个唯一排序键才允许继续往下翻页
结果完整无缺，同 timestamp 的文档内部每次随机排列而已，对翻页完整性无伤大雅
只有 _score 相关性打分会受影响，前后翻页返回的文档集合本身仍然正确
options_en: Tied-timestamp docs have no stable order, so the cursor lands mid-group and some repeat while others are skipped
Elasticsearch rejects the request outright and forces you to add a unique sort key before letting you page further
Results stay complete; tied-timestamp docs merely shuffle randomly within the group, harmless to pagination
Only the _score relevance ranking is affected, and the set of documents returned across pages is still correct
why: search_after 靠「取上一页最后一条 sort 值之后的文档」切页；排序键不唯一时同值文档没有全序，游标切不干净就会跨页重复或漏行。修法：sort 末尾补一个唯一键（如 _id）凑成全序，多存一列换来翻页不重不漏。
why_en: Search_after pages by fetching docs after the previous page's last sort value, so a non-unique sort key leaves tied docs without a total order and the cursor can't split them cleanly — add a unique key like _id to the sort.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用上一页最后一条的 sort 值作为下一页起点的深分页方式，只能向前翻。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Search_after paginates by using the previous page's last sort values as the next page's starting point, moving forward only.

termDefinitions.meaning: 当主排序字段出现相同值时，用来给文档定出唯一先后顺序的附加排序键。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tie-breaker is an extra sort key that assigns a unique order to documents when the main sort field has equal values.

termDefinitions.meaning: Elasticsearch 每个文档的唯一标识，常被拿来当 tie-breaker 保证排序是全序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The _id is Elasticsearch's unique per-document identifier, often used as a tie-breaker to make the sort a total order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文档对查询的相关性得分，默认排序依据，与翻页游标是否唯一无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The _score is a document's relevance score for a query, the default sort key, unrelated to whether the pagination cursor is unique.

q_en: With no unique tie-breaker, how does deep pagination break?
scenario_en: A log search pages through hundreds of thousands of results with search_after; many docs share the same millisecond timestamp, and the engineer sorted only by [timestamp desc] with no _id tie-breaker.
optionExplanations: 同值文档缺全序，游标恰好落在这批中间时，无法判定「之后」是谁，于是这批文档在相邻页里重复或被跳过。
Elasticsearch 不会校验排序键唯一性、也不会拒绝，它照跑，坏结果要到翻页时才暴露。
同值内部顺序不稳定不是「无伤大雅」——正是它导致游标切不干净，进而漏行/重复。
问题出在切页边界而非打分，_score 正确也救不了缺失全序导致的重复与漏行。
optionExplanations_en: Tied docs lack a total order, so when the cursor sits inside that group there's no way to say what comes 'after' — those docs repeat or get skipped across adjacent pages.
Elasticsearch doesn't check sort-key uniqueness or reject the request; it runs, and the bad result only surfaces once you page.
Unstable order within a tie isn't 'harmless' — it's exactly what makes the cursor cut imprecisely and drop or duplicate rows.
The failure is at the page boundary, not in scoring; a correct _score can't fix repeats and gaps caused by a missing total order.

scenario: 商品搜索要在结果上做 faceting（按品类、价格区间统计计数），数据分布在多个 shard 上；团队在纠结是直接基于 Lucene 自建，还是上 Elasticsearch。
q: 跨分片的 faceting/聚合由哪一层提供，这也是选 Elasticsearch 的核心动机之一？
options: Elasticsearch 协调层把各 shard 局部聚合合并成全局 facet，Lucene 不参与
Lucene 内核本身就能跨分片做全局聚合，Elasticsearch 只不过把查询请求原样转发过去罢了而已
由客户端应用层把全部命中文档拉回本地，再自己遍历统计出每一类的计数
由 master 主节点负责，它专门编排聚合任务、并合并来自各分片的局部结果
options_en: Elasticsearch's coordinating layer merges each shard's local aggregation into a global facet; Lucene does none of that
The Lucene core natively performs the global cross-shard aggregation, and Elasticsearch merely forwards the query along
The client application layer pulls every matching document back and then iterates locally to tally each category's count
The master node is responsible, since it is dedicated to orchestrating aggregation tasks and merging each shard's results
why: 聚合/faceting 是 Elasticsearch 编排层的活：协调节点把各 shard 的局部计数合并成全局 facet，Lucene 只管单机内核。需要跨分片 faceting 才选 ES 而非裸 Lucene。
why_en: Aggregation and faceting live in Elasticsearch's orchestration layer — the coordinating node merges each shard's local counts into a global facet, while Lucene only owns the single-node search core, and that's a core reason to pick Elasticsearch over raw Lucene.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给搜索结果按类别、价格区间等维度做计数统计（如电商侧边栏分类计数）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Faceting counts search results by dimensions like category or price range, such as an e-commerce sidebar's per-category counts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对匹配文档做分组统计（计数、求和、分桶）的操作，是 faceting 的底层能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An aggregation groups and summarizes matching documents (counts, sums, buckets) and is the mechanism underneath faceting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收客户端请求、把查询分发到各分片并合并结果的入口节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The coordinating node is the entry point that receives client requests, fans queries out to shards, and merges the results.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引被切分后的一块，1:1 对应一个 Lucene 索引，可分布到不同主机。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shard is one slice of an index, mapped 1:1 to a Lucene index and spread across hosts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责集群级操作（增删节点、建删索引）的协调者，不参与聚合结果的合并。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The master node coordinates cluster-level operations like adding nodes or creating indices, and is not involved in merging aggregation results.

termDefinitions.meaning: Elasticsearch 底层的单机搜索库，负责倒排索引与搜索内核，不做分布式编排。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lucene is the single-node search library under Elasticsearch, owning the inverted index and search core but no distributed orchestration.

q_en: Which layer provides cross-shard faceting/aggregation, one of the core motives for choosing Elasticsearch?
scenario_en: A product search needs faceting on results (counts by category and price band) over data spread across many shards; the team is deciding between building directly on Lucene or adopting Elasticsearch.
optionExplanations: 协调节点收各分片的局部聚合再合并成全局 facet——这层分布式编排正是裸 Lucene 没有、要额外自建的。
Lucene 是单机搜索内核，没有跨分片概念，全局聚合必须由上层协调节点来合并。
把全部命中文档拉回应用层再统计，数据量一大就把网络和内存打爆，正是 ES 要替你省掉的活。
master 只管集群级操作（增删节点/索引），聚合合并是协调节点的职责，别混淆两种节点。
optionExplanations_en: The coordinating node collects each shard's local aggregation and merges it into a global facet — that distributed orchestration is exactly what raw Lucene lacks and you'd have to build.
Lucene is a single-node search core with no notion of shards, so global aggregation must be merged by the coordinating node above it.
Pulling every matching doc back to the app to tally blows up network and memory at scale — precisely the work Elasticsearch saves you.
The master only handles cluster-level operations (adding nodes/indices); merging aggregations is the coordinating node's job — don't conflate the two.

scenario: 商品搜索要在用户用词和商品标题用词不完全一致时也能召回相关商品（按含义/意图匹配），而不只是命中相同的词。
q: 要按「含义」而非「相同词」召回，mapping 里该用哪种字段能力？
options: embedding 字段做语义搜索：按含义相近召回，用词不同也能命中
text 字段配 custom analyzer：把词归一化后进倒排索引，本质仍是共享词元匹配
keyword 字段：把整个值当不可切分的原子，只能做精确相等匹配
加大 from/size 分页深度，多翻几页自然覆盖到语义相近的结果
options_en: An embedding field for semantic search: it recalls by closeness of meaning, matching even when the words differ
A text field with a custom analyzer: it normalizes tokens into the inverted index, but still matches on shared tokens
A keyword field: it treats the whole value as one unsplittable atom and only does exact-equality matching
Increase from/size pagination depth — page further and you'll eventually cover the semantically similar results
tradeoff: 语义召回（embedding） vs 词元精确匹配（analyzer/keyword）
why: 要按含义而非相同词面召回，就需要 embedding 字段做语义搜索；custom analyzer 只是把词归一化后仍进倒排索引，本质还是共享词元匹配。代价：语义召回更重，也可能引入相关性噪声。
why_en: To recall by meaning rather than by identical words you need an embedding field for semantic search; a custom analyzer only normalizes tokens into the inverted index and still relies on shared terms, at the cost of a heavier, noisier recall path.
whenOtherWins: 当用户就是要精确命中相同词（如 SKU、书名、标签），text+analyzer 或 keyword 反而更合适，embedding 的语义召回会引入不相关结果。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把文本编码成数值向量，含义相近的内容在向量空间中距离相近，支撑语义搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding encodes text into a numeric vector so that semantically similar content is close together, enabling semantic search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按含义而非相同词面来召回结果，用词不同也能匹配。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Semantic search retrieves results by meaning rather than identical words, matching even when the wording differs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 定义文本如何被切词和归一化（小写、去词尾等）后写入倒排索引的规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A custom analyzer defines how text is tokenized and normalized (lowercasing, stemming) before it goes into the inverted index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从词到包含该词的文档列表的映射，让关键词查找接近 O(1)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each term to the documents containing it, turning keyword lookup into a near constant-time operation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把整个值当作一个不可切分的原子来索引，用于精确相等匹配和排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A keyword field indexes the whole value as one unsplittable atom, used for exact-match and sorting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 会被分析器切词后进倒排索引的字段类型，用于全文关键词匹配。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A text field is analyzed into tokens in the inverted index and used for full-text keyword matching.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按起始偏移和每页大小分页的方式，只影响返回哪一段结果，与召回什么无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: From/size paginates by start offset and page size; it only affects which slice is returned, not what gets recalled.

q_en: To recall by meaning rather than identical words, which mapping field capability fits?
scenario_en: A product search must recall relevant items even when the user's words and the product title's words don't fully match (matching by meaning/intent), not just hits on identical terms.
optionExplanations: embedding 把文本编码成向量，按含义相近召回，正好解决用词不一致却想匹配意图的场景。
分析器只能做小写、去词尾这类归一化，匹配仍落在共享词元上，用词完全不同就召不回。
keyword 把整值当原子只做精确相等，连近义词都匹配不了，更谈不上语义召回。
分页只决定返回结果的哪一段，召回集合本身没变，翻再多页也变不出语义相近的新文档。
optionExplanations_en: An embedding encodes text into a vector and recalls by closeness of meaning — exactly the case where words differ but you want to match intent.
The analyzer can only lowercase and stem, but matching still rests on shared tokens, so completely different wording won't be recalled.
A keyword field treats the whole value as an atom for exact equality, so it can't even match synonyms, let alone do semantic recall.
Pagination only picks which slice of results to return; the recalled set is unchanged, so paging further never conjures semantically similar new docs.
